title: 1962 Roy Stevens in his barber shop in Dave Howell's pool hall, Jim Hovey in the chair
description: Roy Leonard Stevens, born in 1896, attended Somerville School. At age 17, he began working as a barber in Houlton, Maine. On November 20, 1914, Stevens enlisted in the Canadian Overseas Expeditionary Force and was assigned to the New Brunswick 26th Battalion, which became part of the 5th Infantry Brigade of the Canadian 2nd Division. He served in France and on the Flanders Front from 1915 until the end of the war. In 1919, he married Tessa Aiton and returned to barbering, working first in Florenceville before settling in Hartland for the rest of his career. In the accompanying photo, his barber chair is set up in the front window of David Howell’s pool hall on upper Main Street, where he is shown cutting Jim Hovey’s hair in 1962.
